# mathglyph

> mathglyph is a small, dependency-free text effect for websites. It draws monospace text on one canvas. Letters swap to math glyphs (𝕋 𝒢 ∃ ⊗) and move under the pointer. Version 0.5.0, MIT licence.

Use it for hero headlines, 404 pages and titles. The element keeps its plain text for screen readers, search engines and visitors without JavaScript. mathglyph is not on npm yet: load it from jsDelivr, or install it from GitHub.

- Source and README: https://github.com/8xb300/mathglyph
- Live demo, with a "Copy code" button that prints a working `mount` call: https://8xb300.github.io/mathglyph/
- This file: https://8xb300.github.io/mathglyph/llms.txt

## Install

ES module from the CDN (the core has the `lines` layout and the `breathe` effect):

```js
import { mount, register } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.min.js';
```

Script tag, with the global `MathGlyph` (it also has `MathGlyph.greek`, `MathGlyph.cyrillic` and `MathGlyph.cjk`):

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.iife.min.js"></script>
```

Script tag with every layout and effect already registered:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.all.iife.min.js"></script>
```

From GitHub, with a bundler: `npm install github:8xb300/mathglyph#v0.5.0`. Then `import { mount, register } from 'mathglyph'`, `from 'mathglyph/languages'`, `from 'mathglyph/layouts/ring'` and `from 'mathglyph/effects/firework'`. Types are in `dist/mathglyph.d.ts`, and each module has its own `.d.ts`.

## Minimal mount

Put the plain text in the element. `mount` replaces it with the effect. Without JavaScript, or before the script loads, visitors see the plain text. Words in `*stars*` are highlighted.

```html
<h1 id="hero">Every proof starts with a good guess</h1>
<script type="module">
  import { mount } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.min.js';
  const lines = ['Every proof starts', 'with a *good* guess'];
  mount(document.getElementById('hero'), { lines, palette: 'ice' });
</script>
```

`mount(element, options)` returns an object with four methods:

- `update(options)`: change any option live. Pass only what changes.
- `replay()`: run the decode intro again.
- `reroll()`: pick new glyphs at rest.
- `destroy()`: stop everything and restore the element.

## Plain at rest

With `rest: 'plain'`, the text is plain until the pointer touches it. The glyphs near the pointer wake up. When the pointer leaves, the text goes back to plain.

```js
mount(document.getElementById('hero'), {
  lines: ['every letter is a *variable*', 'and every word, a small *proof*'],
  rest: 'plain',
  revert: 0,  // seconds to wait after the pointer leaves
});
```

## Options

Every option has a default. Pass any of them to `mount`, or to `update`. Shares and rates are numbers from 0 to 1. Distances are in em (1 em is the font size) unless the line says px.

- `lines`: string[], default `['plain text, now with', 'a *math* accent']`. One string per row. `*stars*` highlight a word.
- `layout`: string | { name, ...settings } | Layout, default `'lines'`. One of `'lines'`, `'columns'`, `'grid'`, `'ring'`, or your own layout object.
- `effect`: string | { name, ...settings } | Effect, default `'breathe'`. One of `'breathe'`, `'ripple'`, `'firework'`, `'lens'`, `'cascade'`, `'shatter'`, or your own effect object.
- `scripts`: string[] | object | null, default `null`. Scripts that swaps take look-alike letters from: `['latin', 'greek', 'cyrillic']`, or weights like `{ latin: 2, greek: 1 }`. `null` is Latin only.
- `palette`: string | string[], default `'pastel'`. `'pastel'`, `'ember'`, `'ice'`, `'mono'`, `'shimmer'`, or an array of CSS colours.
- `substitute`: number, default `0.35`. Share of letters swapped at rest.
- `color`: number, default `0.55`. How often glyphs get a palette colour.
- `box`: number, default `0.22`. How often coloured glyphs get a box.
- `boxStyle`: `'detect'` | `'soft'`, default `'detect'`. `'detect'` is a thin 1px rectangle with a label. `'soft'` is a rounded box with a faint fill.
- `boxJitter`: number, default `0.5`. How much boxes vary, from 0 to 1. `0` gives uniform boxes.
- `boxSpan`: number, default `3`. The most neighbouring glyphs one box covers, within a word. `1` gives one glyph per box.
- `labels`: number, default `0.6`. Share of boxes that show a label (`'detect'` only). `0` hides them.
- `labelFormat`: function | null, default `null`. `(cell) => string` for your own label text. `cell` has `glyph`, `char`, `dx`, `width`, `color`, `line` and `column`.
- `symbols`: 'all' | string[], default `'all'`. Symbol groups to use: `general`, `calculus`, `logic`, `linalg`, `numbers`, `geometry`, `statistics`, `physics`, `engineering`, `chemistry`, `cs`, `greek`, `bioastro`, `economics`, `philosophy`, `proofs`, `linguistics`, `law`, `finance`, `category`, `functional`.
- `sets`: object | null, default `null`. Extra symbol groups, `{ name: { symbols, tokens? } }`. You can name them in `symbols`.
- `tokens`: boolean, default `true`. Also swap in short notation like ∫₀, ℏω, ⊗², &&. Only with `expand`.
- `symbolMix`: number, default `0.15`. Share of swaps that use the symbol groups instead of a math-alphabet or Greek version of the same letter.
- `legible`: number, default `0.6`. How often a swapped letter uses a symbol that looks like it (∃ for E, ∪ for U, ∅ for O).
- `lookalikes`: object | null, default `null`. Extra look-alikes, `{ char: 'glyphs' }`. This is also how you plug in the Greek, Cyrillic and CJK tables.
- `words`: number, default `0.7`. How often words with a symbol meaning swap whole (and → ∧, therefore → ∴). Needs `expand`.
- `wordMap`: object | null, default `null`. Extra word → symbol pairs, merged over the English map.
- `motion`: `'hover'` | `'always'` | `'still'`, default `'hover'`. When the effect runs. `'always'` also runs it with a slow wandering point and a slow reshuffle. `'still'` has no animation.
- `rest`: `'glyphs'` | `'plain'`, default `'glyphs'`. `'plain'`: plain text at rest, glyphs only where the pointer touched.
- `revert`: number (seconds), default `0`. With `rest: 'plain'`, how long after the pointer leaves before the text goes back to plain.
- `anchor`: string | true | null, default `null`. A word that never changes and never moves. A string pins its first match. `true` pins the first highlighted word.
- `tracking`: number (em), default `-0.04`. Extra space between letters.
- `wordSpacing`: number (em), default `0.3`. The width of a space.
- `intro`: boolean, default `true`. Left-to-right decode on first show.
- `speed`: number, default `1`. From `0.25` to `2`. How fast the scramble flickers and settles, and how fast slots and lines glide.
- `hoverRadius`: number, default `2.6`. How far the pointer reaches, in character heights.
- `expand`: boolean, default `true`. Each slot widens to fit its glyph. `false` keeps a strict grid.
- `base`: string, default `'#8d8b93'`. Colour of plain text.
- `highlight`: string, default `'#ffffff'`. Colour of highlighted words.
- `font`: string, default a system monospace stack with math fallbacks. A CSS `font-family` stack.
- `fonts`: array, default `[]`. Fonts to load. See Fonts below.
- `fit`: boolean, default `true`. Scale the font so the text fits the container width.
- `maxSize`: number (px), default `44`. Largest font size for `fit`.

## Layouts

`'lines'` is built in. The others are modules: import them and call `register` before `mount`.

```js
import { mount, register } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.min.js';
import { ring } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/layouts/ring.min.js';

register(ring);
mount(document.getElementById('hero'), { layout: { name: 'ring', gap: 2 }, lines: ['every letter goes *round*'] });
```

Modules are at `dist/layouts/<name>.min.js` and `dist/effects/<name>.min.js`, and export one object with the module's name.

- `'lines'`: centred lines. Built in. No settings.
- `'columns'`: vertical text for Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Each line is a column. Settings: `spacing` (1.5, em from one column to the next), `columnOrder` (`'auto'`, or `'rtl'` or `'ltr'`). Set `lang` on the element (`zh-Hans`, `ja`, `ko`). Use 3 or 4 short columns.
- `'grid'`: rows with aligned columns. No settings.
- `'ring'`: the text runs around one circle, clockwise from the top. Settings: `gap` (1, em between two lines). A short phrase of 16 to 28 characters looks best.

## Effects

`effect` sets what the pointer does. `'breathe'` is built in. The others are modules, registered like layouts. Each effect's `speed` is multiplied by the `speed` option. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, no effect runs.

```js
import { mount, register } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/mathglyph.min.js';
import { ripple } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/effects/ripple.min.js';

register(ripple);
const fx = mount(element, { effect: 'ripple' });
fx.update({ effect: { name: 'ripple', speed: 1.5, gap: 3 } });  // settings you leave out keep their defaults
```

- `'breathe'`: glyphs near the pointer scramble and their slots widen. Built in. No settings.
- `'ripple'`: rings run out from the pointer. Settings: `speed` 1, `radius` 5, `gap` 2.5, `pulse` 0.4.
- `'firework'`: glyphs burst outward with sparks, then spring back. Settings: `speed` 1, `radius` 1.7, `power` 0.8, `spin` 0.5 (radians), `sparks` 2.
- `'lens'`: a magnifier follows the pointer. Settings: `speed` 1, `radius` 6, `zoom` 1.8, `swap` true.
- `'cascade'`: letters near the pointer fall into their slots like rain. Settings: `speed` 1, `radius` 3, `fall` 2.5 (at most 3).
- `'shatter'`: letters break into dots, then come together again. Settings: `speed` 1, `radius` 1.8, `scatter` 0.5 (at most 0.6), `dots` 12.

The `radius`, `gap`, `power`, `fall` and `scatter` settings are in em.

## Custom effect

An effect is a plain object. Pass it as `effect`, or pass it to `register` and use its name. Only `name` and `glyph` are required.

```js
const spin = {
  name: 'spin',
  defaults: { radius: 3 },                // settings, in em
  frame: (f) => f.pointer !== null,       // true while the effect still moves something
  glyph(g, out, f) {                      // called for every glyph while frame() returns true
    const d = Math.hypot(g.cx - f.pointer.x, g.cy - f.pointer.y) / (f.settings.radius * f.fs);
    if (d >= 1) return;
    out.rotate = (1 - d) ** 2 * Math.PI;  // out: x, y, scale, rotate, alpha, swap, paint
    out.swap = d < 0.3;
  },
};
mount(element, { effect: spin });
```

- `frame(f)` runs once per frame, before `glyph()`. Return false and the loop sleeps; the engine eases the glyphs back to rest.
- `glyph(g, out, f)` sets `out` for one glyph. `out` resets to rest before each call. `g` is read-only except `g.fx`, which is free for the effect.
- `paint(ctx, g, out, f)` draws extras (sparks, dots). It runs only if `glyph()` set `out.paint = true`.
- `reach` is how far a glyph or its paint goes from its slot, in line heights (default 1).
- `g` has `i`, `line`, `col`, `cx`, `cy`, `w`, `r`, `ch`, `g`, `seed`, `anchor`, `fx`. `f` has `now`, `dt`, `pointer`, `moved`, `radius`, `fs`, `lineH`, `width`, `height`, `speed`, `palette`, `font`, `settings`, `state`, `glyphs`.
- Do not read the DOM in `frame()` or `glyph()`, because that forces a layout. Use `g` and `f`.

The full types are `Effect` and `Layout` in `dist/mathglyph.d.ts`.

## Fonts and languages

The default `font` is a system monospace stack with math fallbacks. Nothing loads from a font CDN. List fonts in `fonts`. Each entry is one of:

- `'IBM Plex Mono'`: a family that the page already provides.
- `{ family: 'IBM Plex Mono', url: '/fonts/plex-mono.woff2' }`: a font file, loaded with the FontFace API.
- `{ family: 'IBM Plex Mono', src: 'url(/fonts/plex-mono-bold.woff2)', weight: '700' }`: a CSS `src` plus FontFace descriptors.

Linux systems often lack math glyphs, and a missing glyph shows as an empty box. The repo has an optional fallback, a Noto Sans Math subset (SIL OFL 1.1): https://github.com/8xb300/mathglyph/blob/main/fonts/noto-sans-math-subset.woff2. Host it with your site:

```js
mount(element, { fonts: [{ family: 'Noto Sans Math', url: '/your/path/noto-sans-math-subset.woff2' }] });
```

Text is split into grapheme clusters with `Intl.Segmenter`, so any script and emoji work. For Greek, Cyrillic and CJK text, plug in the look-alike tables:

```js
import { greek, cyrillic } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/8xb300/mathglyph@v0.5.0/dist/languages.min.js';

mount(element, { lines: ['каждый знак — *переменная*'], lookalikes: { ...greek, ...cyrillic } });
```

`scripts: ['latin', 'greek', 'cyrillic']` mixes Greek and Cyrillic look-alikes into Latin text. `wordMap` adds whole-word swaps in any language that puts spaces between words, and `lookalikes` adds look-alike glyphs. Right-to-left scripts render left to right, and cursive scripts lose their joined forms. Chinese, Japanese and Thai get no whole-word swaps.

## Accessibility

- The canvas is `aria-hidden`. Screen readers and search engines read a visually hidden copy of the plain text, without the stars.
- The element keeps its own role, so an `<h1>` stays a heading.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, there is no intro, no hover scramble, no effect and no reshuffle. With `rest: 'plain'` the text stays plain.
- No timers or frames run while nothing moves, while the text is off screen, or while the tab is hidden.
- Browsers: evergreen. `Intl.Segmenter` is in Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+ and Firefox 125+. Without it, text splits by code point.
